title: Benefits of Java being partially object-oriented
answer: Java is often described as not purely or 100% object-oriented because it includes primitive types such as `int`, `double`, and `boolean` and supports static members that belong to classes rather than object instances. That mixed model is practical: primitives provide compact, efficient value representation for common numeric and boolean operations, while classes, interfaces, inheritance, composition, and polymorphism provide the abstraction and reuse expected from OOP. Wrapper types bridge primitives into object-oriented APIs when an object is required.
